threads.body: This anchored note is inherited only by the total input/output counters. The cache-read, cache-write, and reasoning usage counters each retain separate notes, so the model does not apply the PR's advertised `gen_ai.client.inference.usage.*` failed-operation behavior to the whole counter family. Either apply the rule to those detailed counters too or narrow the PR description, design note, and changelog to the two totals.
threads.hunk:
@@ -18,6 +18,9 @@ metrics:
 
       When systems report both used tokens and billable tokens, instrumentation
       MUST report billable tokens.
+
+      Instrumentation SHOULD record these counters for failed operations too,
+      so that tokens consumed before the failure are still counted.

threads.body: These counters can report used tokens when billable-token data is unavailable, and providers do not necessarily bill tokens from every failed request. Saying the tokens "were still billed" overstates both the metric and provider behavior; base the rationale on cumulative consumption instead.
threads.hunk:
@@ -109,3 +109,11 @@ The two metric families serve different purposes, reflected in their namespaces:
   operations. The `operation` namespace indicates that each measurement represents
   a single operation's token count, producing per-operation distributions and
   percentiles rather than totals.
+
+This split also explains why failed operations are handled differently across
+the two families. Histograms carry no `error.type` dimension, so a failed
+operation's token count would sit in the same distribution as successful ones
+and skew percentiles; instrumentation should skip recording it there. Counters
+exist to track spend, and tokens consumed before a failure were still billed,
+so instrumentation should keep recording them on the counters even when the
+operation ends in an error.

threads.body: The new failed-operation and zero-token branches have no reference coverage. The OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google GenAI scenarios currently record each histogram beside its counter after successful responses; none demonstrates that a successful zero reaches the histogram or that an operation recording `error.type` omits the histogram while retaining counter usage. Add a real SDK scenario for both branches and regenerate its data/report in this PR.

threads.body:
SIG meeting discussion:

Let's make counters and histograms the same.
There could be edge cases for counters when recording 0 could be meaningful now or in the future and it's not worth is to have different logic for counters.

```suggestion
      Instrumentations SHOULD record this metric for each inference operation,
      including failed ones. The recorded value SHOULD match the token count
      returned by the provider, or `0` if the response was not received or
      did not contain token usage.
```
